_comment: Curated metadata for MAME / Arcade entries. Keys are the exact inventory paths from data/inventory.raw.txt. Only verified facts are included; 'verified': false marks an entry whose identity could not be confirmed, in which case year/developer are left out.

arcade/1942.desc: A vertical-scrolling World War II shooter in which a lone P-38 Lightning fights through sixteen stages of Japanese air and naval forces.
arcade/1942.gameplay: Players dodge dense bullet and aircraft patterns while collecting power-ups that widen the fighter's fire. A famous loop-the-loop manoeuvre grants brief invulnerability.
arcade/1942.history: Capcom's first major arcade hit and the start of a long-running series. It was designed by Yoshiki Okamoto, who also created Time Pilot and Gyruss for Konami.

arcade/1942B.desc: An alternate board revision of Capcom's 1942 held in the collection as its own ROM set.

arcade/1943.title: 1943: The Battle of Midway
arcade/1943.desc: A sequel to 1942 that adds an energy meter, a limited special weapon and a boss encounter against the battleship Yamato.

arcade/3STOOGES.title: The Three Stooges
arcade/3STOOGES.desc: An arcade adaptation of the classic comedy trio. The ROM set is present in the collection; release details are not verified.

arcade/ASTDELUX.title: Asteroids Deluxe
arcade/ASTDELUX.desc: Atari's follow-up to Asteroids, adding a shield, smarter saucers and a rotating background that changes the feel of every wave.

arcade/ASTEROID.title: Asteroids
arcade/ASTEROID.desc: A vector-graphics classic in which a tiny ship clears an endless field of drifting rocks that split into smaller, faster fragments.
arcade/ASTEROID.gameplay: The ship drifts with inertia, can hyperspace to escape danger, and must survive escalating waves of asteroids and flying saucers.
arcade/ASTEROID.history: One of the best-selling arcade games of the golden age and a landmark of vector display technology, designed by Lyle Rains and Ed Logg.

arcade/BAGMAN.title: Bagman
arcade/BAGMAN.desc: A thief must haul sacks of loot to the surface while dodging guards and a pursuing policeman in a single-screen mine.

arcade/BAGMANS.title: Super Bagman
arcade/BAGMANS.desc: The sequel to Bagman, expanding the mine with new layouts, faster guards and additional hazards.

arcade/BERZERK.title: Berzerk
arcade/BERZERK.desc: A top-down shooter set in a maze of electrified rooms, where robots hunt the player and the walls themselves can kill.
arcade/BERZERK.history: Berzerk is remembered for its synthesised speech and for being one of the first arcade games with a persistent stalker enemy, Evil Otto.

arcade/BERZERK1.title: Berzerk
arcade/BERZERK1.desc: An alternate board revision of Berzerk preserved as its own ROM set.

arcade/BTIME.title: BurgerTime
arcade/BTIME.desc: Chef Peter Pepper walks across giant burger ingredients, dropping them into place while avoiding anthropomorphic food.
arcade/BTIME.gameplay: Walking the full length of a bun, patty, lettuce or tomato makes it fall one level; crushing enemies scores bonus points but ends their chase only briefly.
arcade/BTIME.history: Designed by Norihiro Kamide for Data East and ported to almost every home system of the early 1980s.

arcade/BTIME2.title: BurgerTime
arcade/BTIME2.desc: A later board revision of BurgerTime kept in the collection as a separate ROM set.

arcade/BTIMEM.title: BurgerTime
arcade/BTIMEM.desc: A further BurgerTime ROM revision present in the collection.

arcade/BWIDOW.title: Black Widow
arcade/BWIDOW.desc: A twin-stick vector shooter in which a spider defends its web from swarms of insects drawn to the centre.

arcade/BZONE.title: Battlezone
arcade/BZONE.desc: A first-person vector tank battle viewed through a periscope, with wireframe terrain, radar and enemy tanks.
arcade/BZONE.history: Originally planned as a military training tool, Battlezone became a landmark of 3D arcade graphics. Atari later produced a Bradley Trainer variant for the US Army.

arcade/CARNIVAL.title: Carnival
arcade/CARNIVAL.desc: Players shoot rows of targets at a fairground shooting gallery, protecting a limited supply of bullets from mischievous ducks.

arcade/CCASTLES.title: Crystal Castles
arcade/CCASTLES.desc: Bentley Bear collects gems through isometric castles while dodging bees, skeletons and a bouncing hat.

arcade/CCASTLE2.title: Crystal Castles
arcade/CCASTLE2.desc: An alternate Crystal Castles board revision preserved in the collection.

arcade/CCLIMBER.title: Crazy Climber
arcade/CCLIMBER.desc: A climber scales the face of a skyscraper using a pair of joysticks, dodging falling flowerpots and closing windows.
arcade/CCLIMBER.history: Notable for its dual-joystick control scheme, which let each hand move independently and gave the game an unusually physical feel.

arcade/CENTIPED.title: Centipede
arcade/CENTIPED.desc: A bug shooter set in a field of mushrooms, where a centipede splits into faster segments as it is hit.
arcade/CENTIPED.gameplay: The player's ship is confined to the lower fifth of the screen; poisoning mushrooms sends the centipede into a wild dive toward the player.
arcade/CENTIPED.history: Designed by Ed Logg and Dona Bailey, one of the first arcade games designed by a woman and a huge early-1980s success.

arcade/CENTIPD2.title: Centipede
arcade/CENTIPD2.desc: An alternate Centipede ROM revision held in the collection.

arcade/CIRCUSC.title: Circus Charlie
arcade/CIRCUSC.desc: A circus performer rides a lion through flaming hoops, walks a tightrope and bounces on a trampoline across six mini-games.

arcade/CONGO.title: Congo Bongo
arcade/CONGO.desc: An isometric jungle climb in which an explorer chases a gorilla up a mountain, avoiding monkeys, coconuts and gaps.

arcade/CRUSH.title: Crush Roller
arcade/CRUSH.desc: A paint-roller maze game in which a roller covers every path while fish-like enemies give chase.

arcade/DEFENDER.title: Defender
arcade/DEFENDER.desc: A horizontal shooter across a scrolling alien landscape, protecting humanoids from abduction while managing a dangerous radar map.
arcade/DEFENDER.gameplay: The ship can reverse direction and warp across the world; losing all humanoids turns the planet into a minefield and eventually ends the game.
arcade/DEFENDER.history: Designed by Eugene Jarvis and Larry DeMar, Defender set the template for the modern action arcade game and was notoriously difficult.

arcade/DEFENDG.title: Defender
arcade/DEFENDG.desc: The 'green label' board revision of Defender, preserved as its own ROM set.

arcade/DIAMOND.title: Diamond Run
arcade/DIAMOND.desc: An isometric arcade action game held in the collection under the ROM identifier DIAMOND. Release details are not verified.

arcade/DIGDUG.title: Dig Dug
arcade/DIGDUG.desc: A underground gardener tunnels through soil, inflating and popping enemies with a pump or crushing them with falling rocks.
arcade/DIGDUG.history: One of Namco's defining early titles, designed by Masahisa Ikegami with character art by Hiroshi Ono.

arcade/DKONG.title: Donkey Kong
arcade/DKONG.desc: Mario climbs girders to rescue Pauline from a barrel-throwing gorilla in the game that established the platform genre.
arcade/DKONG.gameplay: Four single-screen stages — barrels, rivets, springs and conveyors — must be cleared in sequence, each faster than the last.
arcade/DKONG.history: Designed by Shigeru Miyamoto with programming by Ikegami Tsushinki, Donkey Kong introduced Mario (then Jumpman) and became Nintendo's first big arcade success.

arcade/DKONG31.title: Donkey Kong 3
arcade/DKONG31.desc: A variant ROM set of Donkey Kong 3, the greenhouse shooter starring Stanley the exterminator.

arcade/ELEVATOR.title: Elevator Action
arcade/ELEVATOR.desc: A spy descends a skyscraper by elevator and escalator, collecting secret documents while enemy agents open fire.

arcade/FROGGER.title: Frogger
arcade/FROGGER.desc: A frog crosses a busy highway and a log-filled river to reach its home lily pads, one hop at a time.
arcade/FROGGER.gameplay: Timing and lane reading define the challenge; each of five homes must be filled, and a timer adds pressure to every crossing.
arcade/FROGGER.history: Created by Akira Hashimoto at Konami and licensed to Sega for arcade distribution, Frogger became a pop-culture staple of the 1980s.

arcade/GALAGA.title: Galaga
arcade/GALAGA.desc: A fixed shooter in which insectoid aliens swoop in formation; a captured fighter can be rescued to double your firepower.
arcade/GALAGA.gameplay: Enemies dive in curved attack runs. Letting a boss Galaga tractor-beam your ship and then shooting the captor reunites the two fighters for double shots.
arcade/GALAGA.history: The sequel to Galaxian and one of the most successful arcade games ever made, celebrated for its choreographed enemy patterns and challenging stages.

arcade/GALAGA88.title: Galaga '88
arcade/GALAGA88.desc: A late-1980s Galaga sequel with scrolling stages, warp gates and a branching path through the game.

arcade/GALAXIAN.title: Galaxian
arcade/GALAXIAN.desc: The direct predecessor of Galaga, introducing full-colour sprites and enemies that peel out of formation to dive at the player.
arcade/GALAXIAN.history: Galaxian was one of the first colour arcade games and a deliberate response to Space Invaders' monochrome look.

arcade/GAUNTLET.title: Gauntlet
arcade/GAUNTLET.desc: Four-player dungeon crawling with health that constantly drains, monsters that spawn endlessly and walls that must be shot open.
arcade/GAUNTLET.gameplay: Warrior, Valkyrie, Wizard and Elf each have distinct strengths; food restores health and the famous narrator comments on every event.
arcade/GAUNTLET.history: A coin-op landmark for four-player co-operative play, designed by Ed Logg and later ported widely.

arcade/GAUNT2.title: Gauntlet II
arcade/GAUNT2.desc: A Gauntlet II ROM set preserved in the collection.

arcade/gaunt2.zip.title: Gauntlet II
arcade/gaunt2.zip.desc: The zipped Gauntlet II ROM set held alongside the unpacked folder.

arcade/gauntlet.zip.title: Gauntlet
arcade/gauntlet.zip.desc: The zipped Gauntlet ROM set held alongside the unpacked folder.

arcade/GOLDNAXE.title: Golden Axe
arcade/GOLDNAXE.desc: A side-scrolling fantasy beat-'em-up in which three heroes fight Death Adder's soldiers, riding beasts and casting magic.
arcade/GOLDNAXE.history: A major Sega System 16 title that became one of the Mega Drive's signature games.

arcade/GORF.title: Gorf
arcade/GORF.desc: A five-stage space shooter that borrows mechanics from Astro Blaster, Space Invaders, Galaxian and Wizard of Wor in sequence.
arcade/GORF.history: Gorf was an early arcade game to use synthesised speech, taunting the player with lines like 'Prepare yourself for a galactic war'.'

arcade/gorf.zip.title: Gorf
arcade/gorf.zip.desc: The zipped Gorf ROM set held alongside the unpacked folder.

arcade/GYRUSS.title: Gyruss
arcade/GYRUSS.desc: A tube shooter in which the player orbits Earth, moving in a circle while waves of enemies stream inward from deep space.
arcade/GYRUSS.history: Designed by Yoshiki Okamoto and notable for its Bach-inspired soundtrack and pseudo-3D starfield.

arcade/GYRUSSCE.title: Gyruss
arcade/GYRUSSCE.desc: The Centuri-licensed release of Gyruss, held as a separate ROM set.

arcade/INVADERS.title: Space Invaders
arcade/INVADERS.desc: The game that launched the arcade boom: rows of aliens descend while the player's laser cannon picks them off from behind four shields.
arcade/INVADERS.gameplay: The aliens speed up as their numbers thin, and the player must manage a single cannon against an ever-descending formation.
arcade/INVADERS.history: Designed by Tomohiro Nishikado, Space Invaders triggered the golden age of arcade video games and made Taito a household name.

arcade/IROBOT.title: I, Robot
arcade/IROBOT.desc: A polygonal 3D shooter in which a player guides a robot through geometric worlds while being watched by the evil eye.
arcade/IROBOT.history: One of the first arcade games with fully filled 3D polygons and an early example of a game designed around a 'not for kids' theme.

arcade/JOURNEY.title: Journey
arcade/JOURNEY.desc: A music-themed arcade game featuring the band Journey, mixing mini-games with digitised concert footage and their music.

arcade/JOUST.title: Joust
arcade/JOUST.desc: Knights on flying ostriches collide in mid-air; the higher lance wins, and defeated riders drop eggs that must be collected.
arcade/JOUST.gameplay: Flap to gain altitude, build momentum and strike from above. A pterodactyl arrives if a wave drags on too long.
arcade/JOUST.history: Designed by John Newcomer, Joust is remembered for its two-player co-operation and its unusual physics-based aerial combat.

arcade/JOUSTR.title: Joust
arcade/JOUSTR.desc: An alternate Joust ROM revision preserved in the collection.

arcade/JOUSTWR.title: Joust
arcade/JOUSTWR.desc: A further Joust ROM revision (white-label set) held in the collection.

arcade/JRPACMAN.title: Jr. Pac-Man
arcade/JRPACMAN.desc: A scrolling Pac-Man sequel in which Jr. Pac-Man clears wider mazes while his bicycle-riding enemies grow faster with each level.

arcade/KLAX.title: Klax
arcade/KLAX.desc: A tile-matching puzzle game in which coloured bricks roll down a conveyor and must be caught and arranged into lines.

arcade/LADYBUG.title: Lady Bug
arcade/LADYBUG.desc: A maze game with rotating doors and collectible letters, inspired by Pac-Man but built around a different scoring system.

arcade/LDRUN.title: Lode Runner
arcade/LDRUN.desc: A platform puzzle in which a runner collects gold and digs traps to contain pursuing guards.

arcade/MAKETRAX.title: Make Trax
arcade/MAKETRAX.desc: A paint-roller maze game (released in Japan as Crush Roller) in which the player paints every path while avoiding fish.

arcade/MAPPY.title: Mappy
arcade/MAPPY.desc: A police mouse bounces between trampolines and doors, recovering stolen goods from a gang of cats.

arcade/MATMANIA.title: Mat Mania
arcade/MATMANIA.desc: A colourful wrestling game with exaggerated moves and a cast of flamboyant opponents.

arcade/MILLIPED.title: Millipede
arcade/MILLIPED.desc: The sequel to Centipede, adding earwigs, spiders, beetles and a wider range of mushroom-shooting tactics.

arcade/MISSILE.title: Missile Command
arcade/MISSILE.desc: A trackball-controlled defence game in which three missile batteries protect six cities from an endless nuclear barrage.
arcade/MISSILE.gameplay: Every interception costs valuable ammunition, and the attack accelerates relentlessly; the game ends when all six cities are lost.
arcade/MISSILE.history: Designed by Dave Theurer, Missile Command is remembered for its Cold War theme and its intense, escalating difficulty.

arcade/MPATROL.title: Moon Patrol
arcade/MPATROL.desc: A buggy rolls across the lunar surface, jumping craters and firing at alien craft while a two-axis parallax background scrolls behind.

arcade/MPATROLW.title: Moon Patrol
arcade/MPATROLW.desc: The Williams-licensed release of Moon Patrol, preserved as a separate ROM set.

arcade/MRDOT.title: Mr. Do!
arcade/MRDOT.desc: A clown digs tunnels through an orchard, dropping apples on enemies or eliminating them with a power ball.

arcade/mrdo.title: Mr. Do!
arcade/mrdo.desc: A Mr. Do! ROM set held in the collection.

arcade/MSPACMAN.title: Ms. Pac-Man
arcade/MSPACMAN.desc: A faster, more varied Pac-Man with four mazes, moving bonus fruit and smarter ghosts.
arcade/MSPACMAN.history: Originally an unauthorised enhancement kit, Ms. Pac-Man was licensed by Midway and became one of the most successful arcade games in North America.

arcade/OUTRUNA.title: Out Run
arcade/OUTRUNA.desc: A behind-the-car driving game with a Ferrari Testarossa, branching routes and a selectable radio soundtrack.

arcade/outrun.title: Out Run
arcade/outrun.desc: An Out Run ROM set held in the collection.

arcade/PACHEART.title: Pac-Man (PACHEART ROM set)
arcade/PACHEART.desc: An arcade Pac-Man-family ROM set held under the identifier PACHEART. The exact revision has not been verified.

arcade/PACLAND.title: Pac-Land
arcade/PACLAND.desc: A side-scrolling Pac-Man platformer with a scrolling world, a fairy companion and a pogo-stick finale.

arcade/PACMAN.title: Pac-Man
arcade/PACMAN.desc: The maze-chase landmark: eat every dot, avoid four ghosts, and turn the tables with a Power Pellet.
arcade/PACMAN.gameplay: Each ghost has its own targeting behaviour — Blinky chases, Pinky ambushes, Inky is unpredictable and Clyde keeps his distance. Bonus fruit appears near the centre.
arcade/PACMAN.history: Designed by Toru Iwatani, Pac-Man was conceived as a game that would appeal to players beyond the shooter crowd and became the best-selling arcade machine of all time.

arcade/PACMANIA.title: Pac-Mania
arcade/PACMANIA.desc: An isometric Pac-Man sequel in which the player can jump over ghosts, with scrolling mazes and a rendered 3D look.

arcade/PACMANJP.title: Pac-Man
arcade/PACMANJP.desc: The Japanese release of Pac-Man (Puck Man), preserved as a separate ROM set.

arcade/PACPLUS.title: Pac-Man Plus
arcade/PACPLUS.desc: A modified Pac-Man released as an upgrade kit, with invisible mazes, altered ghost behaviour and new bonus items.

arcade/PENGO.title: Pengo
arcade/PENGO.desc: A penguin pushes blocks of ice across a maze to crush pursuing Sno-Bees, with a time-limited bonus round.

arcade/PHOENIXT.title: Phoenix
arcade/PHOENIXT.desc: A fixed shooter with five distinct stages, including a mothership boss and a notorious flock of small birds.
arcade/PHOENIXT.history: Phoenix was one of the first arcade games to feature a boss battle at the end of a stage sequence.

arcade/phoenix.title: Phoenix
arcade/phoenix.desc: A Phoenix ROM set held in the collection.

arcade/PITFALL2.title: Pitfall II: Lost Caverns
arcade/PITFALL2.desc: An arcade adaptation of the Atari 2600 exploration game, with Pitfall Harry searching underground caverns for his niece and a diamond.

arcade/PITFIGHT.title: Pit Fighter
arcade/PITFIGHT.desc: A digitised-actor fighting game with three selectable brawlers and a chain of increasingly tough opponents.

arcade/QBERT.title: Q*bert
arcade/QBERT.desc: An orange creature hops across an isometric pyramid, changing the colour of every cube while dodging Coily and his friends.
arcade/QBERT.history: Designed by Warren Davis and Jeff Lee, Q*bert is one of the most recognisable arcade characters of the early 1980s.

arcade/QBERTQUB.title: Q*bert's Qubes
arcade/QBERTQUB.desc: A Q*bert sequel in which cubes must be rotated to match a target pattern, adding a colour-matching puzzle layer.

arcade/QIX.title: Qix
arcade/QIX.desc: A minimalist area-capture game: draw boxes across an empty field while avoiding a swirling, unpredictable Qix.

arcade/QIX2.title: Qix II: Tournament
arcade/QIX2.desc: A tournament revision of Qix with altered scoring and faster play.

arcade/RALLYX.title: Rally-X
arcade/RALLYX.desc: A driving maze game in which a blue car collects flags while evading red pursuers, with a limited smoke-screen defence.
arcade/RALLYX.history: Rally-X introduced scrolling mazes and a radar map to the arcade, both later reused in Pac-Man.

arcade/RALLYXM.title: Rally-X
arcade/RALLYXM.desc: The Midway-licensed version of Rally-X, preserved as a separate ROM set.

arcade/ROBOTRON.title: Robotron: 2084
arcade/ROBOTRON.desc: A twin-stick survival shooter in which a lone human must rescue the last family on Earth from relentless robot hordes.
arcade/ROBOTRON.gameplay: One stick moves, the other fires in any direction; the screen fills with enemies and the pace only increases.
arcade/ROBOTRON.history: Designed by Eugene Jarvis and Larry DeMar, Robotron is regarded as the definitive twin-stick shooter and a landmark of pure arcade design.

arcade/SBAGMAN.title: Super Bagman
arcade/SBAGMAN.desc: The sequel to Bagman, expanding the mine with new layouts and faster guards.

arcade/SHINOBI.title: Shinobi
arcade/SHINOBI.desc: A ninja rescues hostages from a terrorist organisation, using shuriken, a sword and a limited-use ninja magic.
arcade/SHINOBI.history: A Sega System 16 hit that spawned a long series and helped define the modern action-platformer.

arcade/shinobi.zip.title: Shinobi
arcade/shinobi.zip.desc: The zipped Shinobi ROM set held alongside the unpacked folder.

arcade/SINISTAR.title: Sinistar
arcade/SINISTAR.desc: A miner gathers crystals to build bombs while a growing mechanical voice announces the arrival of the planet-devouring Sinistar.
arcade/SINISTAR.history: Sinistar was an early arcade game with a dynamic camera and one of the first to use stereo sound and digitised speech.

arcade/SPELUNKR.title: Spelunker
arcade/SPELUNKR.desc: A fragile explorer descends into caverns to collect treasure, dying from even a short fall.

arcade/SPYHUNT.title: Spy Hunter
arcade/SPYHUNT.desc: A spy car races up a scrolling highway, deploying oil slicks and smoke screens while a weapons van upgrades its arsenal.
arcade/SPYHUNT.history: Spy Hunter's Peter Gunn-inspired soundtrack and convertible car gimmick made it one of Midway's most enduring titles.

arcade/SQBERT.title: Faster, Harder, More Challenging Q*bert
arcade/SQBERT.desc: A harder revision of Q*bert with faster enemies and revised level layouts, sometimes known as S.Q. Bert.

arcade/STARCAS.title: Star Castle
arcade/STARCAS.desc: A vector shooter in which a rotating fortress of rings must be peeled away to reach the cannon at its centre.

arcade/STARGATE.title: Stargate
arcade/STARGATE.desc: The sequel to Defender, adding an inviso-cloak, a stargate warp and new enemy types across a more complex landscape.

arcade/STARWARS.title: Star Wars
arcade/STARWARS.desc: A vector-graphics rail shooter recreating the Death Star trench run, with digitised speech sampled from the film.

arcade/SUPBTIME.title: Super BurgerTime
arcade/SUPBTIME.desc: A late sequel to BurgerTime with larger sprites, new enemies and two-player simultaneous play.

arcade/SUPERPAC.title: Super Pac-Man
arcade/SUPERPAC.desc: A Pac-Man sequel with doors, keys and a super-size power-up that lets Pac-Man smash through ghosts.

arcade/TAPPER.title: Tapper
arcade/TAPPER.desc: A bartender slides drinks down four counters while collecting empty glasses, with a later root-beer variant for family audiences.

arcade/TEMPEST.title: Tempest
arcade/TEMPEST.desc: A colour vector shooter fought on the rim of a deep well, with a spinner controller and sixteen abstract tube designs.
arcade/TEMPEST.history: Designed by Dave Theurer, Tempest is celebrated for its vector graphics, fast difficulty curve and unique rotary control.

arcade/THEEND.title: The End
arcade/THEEND.desc: A space shooter in which the player defends a base at the bottom of the screen from waves of attackers.

arcade/THEENDS.title: The End
arcade/THEENDS.desc: An alternate The End ROM set preserved in the collection.

arcade/TIMEPLT.title: Time Pilot
arcade/TIMEPLT.desc: A free-scrolling shooter in which the player's plane flies through five eras, from 1910 biplanes to 2001 UFOs.

arcade/TOOBIN.title: Toobin'
arcade/TOOBIN.desc: A river-rafting game in which two players steer inner tubes downstream, throwing cans at obstacles and each other.

arcade/TRACKFLD.title: Track & Field
arcade/TRACKFLD.desc: A button-mashing athletics game covering sprinting, hurdles, long jump, javelin and hammer throw.

arcade/TRON.title: Tron
arcade/TRON.desc: A four-stage arcade adaptation of the film, mixing light-cycle racing, grid-bug shooting and a recogniser battle.

arcade/VENTURE.title: Venture
arcade/VENTURE.desc: A dungeon crawler with an overhead map and room-by-room combat, in which a treasure hunter raids four monster-filled vaults.

arcade/WARRIOR.title: Warrior
arcade/WARRIOR.desc: A one-on-one vector sword-fighting game often cited as the first versus fighting game.

arcade/WOW.title: Wizard of Wor
arcade/WOW.desc: A two-player maze shooter in which warriors hunt monsters in a dark dungeon, with a 'worluk' bonus round.

arcade/XEVIOUSA.title: Xevious
arcade/XEVIOUSA.desc: A vertically scrolling shooter with separate air and ground weapons, and hidden special flags to uncover.
arcade/XEVIOUSA.history: Xevious is often credited as the first vertically scrolling shooter with a distinct ground layer.

arcade/ZAXXON.title: Zaxxon
arcade/ZAXXON.desc: An isometric shooter with a pseudo-3D fortress, altitude-based dodging and a notorious robot boss.

arcade/aliens.title: Aliens
arcade/aliens.desc: A side-scrolling run-and-gun adaptation of the film, with two-player co-op and a motion tracker.

arcade/aliensj.zip.title: Aliens
arcade/aliensj.zip.desc: The Japanese release of Konami's Aliens, preserved as a separate ROM set.

arcade/arcadecl.title: Arcade Classics (ROM set)
arcade/arcadecl.desc: A compiled arcade ROM set held under the identifier ARCADECL. Its exact contents and release details are not verified.

arcade/atarifb.title: Atari Football
arcade/atarifb.desc: A black-and-white trackball football game, one of the first to use a trackball and a scrolling playfield.

arcade/atarifb4.title: Atari Football (4-player)
arcade/atarifb4.desc: The four-player cabinet version of Atari Football, with a wider control panel and a larger trackball layout.

arcade/bowlrama.title: Bowl-O-Rama
arcade/bowlrama.desc: A bowling arcade title held in the collection. Release details are not verified.

arcade/bubbles.title: Bubbles
arcade/bubbles.desc: A top-down game in which a soap bubble cleans a sink by absorbing dirt, growing larger and more vulnerable as it does.

arcade/bublbobl.title: Bubble Bobble
arcade/bublbobl.desc: Two dragons trap enemies in bubbles and pop them across a hundred single-screen stages, with branching routes and co-op play.

arcade/citycon.title: City Connection
arcade/citycon.desc: A car paints every road in a city while evading police, jumping between highways and collecting icons.

arcade/cloak.title: Cloak & Dagger
arcade/cloak.desc: A top-down spy shooter tied to the film of the same name, with four distinct multi-screen levels.

arcade/commsega.title: Commando (ROM set)
arcade/commsega.desc: A Commando-family ROM set held under the identifier COMMSEGA. The exact regional revision is not verified.

arcade/dkong3.title: Donkey Kong 3
arcade/dkong3.desc: A greenhouse shooter in which Stanley sprays insecticide at Donkey Kong and his swarm of bugs.

arcade/dkongjr.title: Donkey Kong Jr.
arcade/dkongjr.desc: Donkey Kong's son climbs vines and chains to free his caged father, avoiding snapjaws and birds.

arcade/docastle.title: Mr. Do's Castle
arcade/docastle.desc: A Mr. Do! spin-off set in a castle of platforms, where the clown flips floor tiles to trap unicorns.

arcade/docastl2.title: Mr. Do's Castle
arcade/docastl2.desc: An alternate Mr. Do's Castle ROM set held in the collection.

arcade/dorunrun.title: Do! Run Run
arcade/dorunrun.desc: A Mr. Do! sequel in which the clown rolls logs around a maze to crush enemies and collect points.

arcade/dotron.title: Discs of Tron
arcade/dotron.desc: A one-on-one disc duel set inside the Tron universe, with a parallax arena and an escalating series of opponents.

arcade/dowild.title: Wild Western
arcade/dowild.desc: A Western-themed ROM set held under the identifier DOWILD. The title and release details are not verified.

arcade/fitegolf.title: Fighting Golf
arcade/fitegolf.desc: An arcade golf game with a three-click swing meter and competitive match play.

arcade/frenzy.title: Frenzy
arcade/frenzy.desc: The sequel to Berzerk, adding destructible walls, new robot types and a level progression system.

arcade/junglek.title: Jungle King
arcade/junglek.desc: A jungle adventure in which a explorer swings on vines, swims past crocodiles and rescues a captured companion.

arcade/kangaroo.title: Kangaroo
arcade/kangaroo.desc: A mother kangaroo punches and climbs her way up a zoo to rescue her joey from monkeys.

arcade/kchamp.title: Karate Champ
arcade/kchamp.desc: A one-on-one karate game with twin joysticks and a wide set of directional moves, predating Street Fighter.

arcade/kick.title: Kick
arcade/kick.desc: A clown balances on a unicycle and catches falling balloons in this early Bally Midway title.

arcade/mario.title: Mario Bros.
arcade/mario.desc: Mario and Luigi clear a sewer of turtles and crabs by bumping them from below and kicking them away.

arcade/mooncrst.title: Moon Cresta
arcade/mooncrst.desc: A fixed shooter in which three dockable ship sections can be combined, with difficulty rising as sections are lost.

arcade/paperboy.title: Paperboy
arcade/paperboy.desc: A paperboy cycles a suburban street, throwing newspapers at subscribers while dodging dogs, cars and lawnmowers.

arcade/pigskin.title: Pigskin 621 A.D.
arcade/pigskin.desc: A violent medieval football game with no rules beyond carrying the ball to the goal.

arcade/polepos.title: Pole Position
arcade/polepos.desc: A behind-the-car Formula One racer with a qualifying lap and a Fuji Speedway circuit.
arcade/polepos.history: Pole Position popularised the racing game genre and introduced the qualifying-lap structure still used today.

arcade/polepos2.title: Pole Position II
arcade/polepos2.desc: A sequel to Pole Position with four selectable tracks and improved car handling.

arcade/popeye.title: Popeye
arcade/popeye.desc: Popeye collects hearts and spinach while Bluto pursues Olive Oyl across a three-level stage.

arcade/punchout.title: Punch-Out!!
arcade/punchout.desc: A boxing game with two oversized monitors and a cast of cartoon opponents, each with readable tells.

arcade/shollow.title: Satan's Hollow
arcade/shollow.desc: A shooter in which the player builds a bridge across a lava-filled chasm while gargoyles attack from both sides.

arcade/simpsons.title: The Simpsons
arcade/simpsons.desc: A four-player beat-'em-up in which the Simpsons rescue Maggie from Smithers and Mr. Burns.

arcade/snakepit.title: Snake Pit
arcade/snakepit.desc: A snake-handling game in which a explorer runs through a temple, using a snake to defeat hostile creatures.

arcade/spnchout.title: Super Punch-Out!!
arcade/spnchout.desc: A refined Punch-Out!! with a transparent player sprite, new opponents and a faster pace.

arcade/tagteam.title: Tag Team Wrestling
arcade/tagteam.desc: A tag-team wrestling game with two-player co-op and a colourful cast of masked wrestlers.

arcade/tagteam.zip.title: Tag Team Wrestling
arcade/tagteam.zip.desc: The zipped Tag Team Wrestling ROM set held alongside the unpacked folder.

arcade/yard.title: 10-Yard Fight
arcade/yard.desc: An American football game with a vertical scrolling field and a simple playbook.

arcade/zookeep.title: Zoo Keeper
arcade/zookeep.desc: A zookeeper runs around a zoo enclosure, jumping over animals and rescuing a escaped monkey while a timer runs down.

arcade/720.zip.title: 720°
arcade/720.zip.desc: A skateboarding game built around a rotational joystick, with a large scrolling skate park and a map screen.

arcade/airwolf.zip.title: Airwolf
arcade/airwolf.zip.desc: A horizontal helicopter shooter based on the television series, with a recharging cannon and missile sub-weapon.

arcade/aliensyn.zip.title: Alien Syndrome
arcade/aliensyn.zip.desc: A top-down run-and-gun in which two players rescue hostages from an infested space station before a timer expires.

arcade/apb.zip.title: A.P.B.
arcade/apb.zip.desc: A police driving game in which an officer issues tickets and chases suspects across a scrolling city.

arcade/archrivl.zip.title: Arch Rivals
arcade/archrivl.zip.desc: A two-on-two basketball game with no fouls, built for shoving opponents and dunking on a scrolling court.

arcade/arkanoi2.zip.title: Arkanoid: Revenge of Doh
arcade/arkanoi2.zip.desc: The sequel to Arkanoid, adding enemies that fire at the paddle and a final boss, Doh.

arcade/ark2jp.zip.title: Arkanoid: Revenge of Doh
arcade/ark2jp.zip.desc: The Japanese release of Arkanoid: Revenge of Doh.

arcade/arkanoid.zip.title: Arkanoid
arcade/arkanoid.zip.desc: A breakout-style brick breaker with power-up capsules, angled paddle physics and a boss encounter.
arcade/arkanoid.zip.history: Arkanoid refined the Breakout formula and became one of Taito's most ported arcade games.

arcade/armwrest.zip.title: Arm Wrestling
arcade/armwrest.zip.desc: A dual-screen arm-wrestling game with a rotating joystick and a cast of cartoon opponents.

arcade/basebal2.zip.title: Baseball (ROM set BASEBAL2)
arcade/basebal2.zip.desc: A baseball arcade ROM set held under the identifier BASEBAL2. Exact release details are not verified.

arcade/bladestl.zip.title: Blade Steeler (ROM set)
arcade/bladestl.zip.desc: An arcade title held under the identifier BLADESTL. The title and release details are not verified.

arcade/bsktball.zip.title: Basketball (ROM set)
arcade/bsktball.zip.desc: A basketball arcade ROM set held under the identifier BSKTBALL. Release details are not verified.

arcade/bssoccer.zip.title: Soccer (ROM set BSSOCCER)
arcade/bssoccer.zip.desc: A soccer arcade ROM set held under the identifier BSSOCCER. Release details are not verified.

arcade/cavenger.zip.title: Cosmic Avenger
arcade/cavenger.zip.desc: A horizontal shooter with a colourful landscape, ground targets and a scrolling cave section.

arcade/cclimbr2.zip.title: Crazy Climber 2
arcade/cclimbr2.zip.desc: The sequel to Crazy Climber, adding new buildings, weather hazards and cooperative climbing.

arcade/chopper.zip.title: Chopper I
arcade/chopper.zip.desc: A vertical helicopter shooter held in the collection. Release year is not verified.

arcade/chplft.zip.title: Choplifter
arcade/chplft.zip.desc: A rescue helicopter picks up hostages from hostile territory while dodging tanks, jets and anti-aircraft fire.

arcade/clowns.zip.title: Clowns
arcade/clowns.zip.desc: A black-and-white balloon-popping game in which two clowns walk a tightrope and swing across the screen.

arcade/cop01.zip.title: Cop 01
arcade/cop01.zip.desc: An arcade action title held under the identifier COP01. Release details are not verified.

arcade/copsnrob.zip.title: Cops'n Robbers
arcade/copsnrob.zip.desc: A top-down driving shooter in which a police car chases robbers through city streets.

arcade/ddragon.zip.title: Double Dragon
arcade/ddragon.zip.desc: A side-scrolling beat-'em-up in which two brothers rescue Marian from the Black Warriors gang.
arcade/ddragon.zip.history: Double Dragon defined the co-operative beat-'em-up formula and became one of the most influential arcade games of the late 1980s.

arcade/ddragon2.zip.title: Double Dragon II: The Revenge
arcade/ddragon2.zip.desc: A sequel with a directional attack system, new stages and a revenge plot after Marian's death.

arcade/ddragon3.zip.title: Double Dragon 3: The Rosetta Stone
arcade/ddragon3.zip.desc: The third Double Dragon, adding shops where players buy moves and items with real credits.

arcade/digdug2.zip.title: Dig Dug II
arcade/digdug2.zip.desc: A sequel set on an island, where Dig Dug drills fault lines to sink sections of land into the sea.

arcade/digger.zip.title: Digger
arcade/digger.zip.desc: An arcade digging game held under the identifier DIGGER. Release details are not verified.

arcade/dino.zip.title: Cadillacs and Dinosaurs
arcade/dino.zip.desc: A four-player beat-'em-up based on the Xenozoic Tales comic, with dinosaurs, vehicles and a post-apocalyptic city.

arcade/dinorex.zip.title: Dino Rex
arcade/dinorex.zip.desc: A dinosaur-versus-dinosaur fighting game with digitised sprite artwork and a prehistoric tournament framing.

arcade/empcity.zip.title: Empire City: 1931
arcade/empcity.zip.desc: A vertical shooter in which a 1930s gangster fires from a car window at pursuing rivals and police.

arcade/empcityj.zip.title: Empire City: 1931
arcade/empcityj.zip.desc: The Japanese release of Empire City: 1931.

arcade/empire.zip.title: Empire (ROM set)
arcade/empire.zip.desc: An arcade ROM set held under the identifier EMPIRE. The exact title and release details are not verified.

arcade/foodf.zip.title: Food Fight
arcade/foodf.zip.desc: A chef collects ice cream while dodging food-throwing opponents in an isometric arena.

arcade/ftsoccer.zip.title: Soccer (ROM set FTSOCCER)
arcade/ftsoccer.zip.desc: A soccer arcade ROM set held under the identifier FTSOCCER. Release details are not verified.

arcade/gghost.zip.title: Golly! Ghost!
arcade/gghost.zip.desc: A light-gun game in which players shoot ghosts in a haunted house, with a mechanical backdrop.

arcade/ghostb.zip.title: The Real Ghostbusters
arcade/ghostb.zip.desc: A top-down shooter based on the animated series, with three playable Ghostbusters and a vacuum weapon.

arcade/ghouls.zip.title: Ghouls'n Ghosts
arcade/ghouls.zip.desc: The sequel to Ghosts'n Goblins, with Arthur again fighting through demonic stages to save Prin-Prin.

arcade/gng.zip.title: Ghosts'n Goblins
arcade/gng.zip.desc: A punishing platformer in which knight Arthur battles the undead to rescue Prin-Prin, losing his armour in one hit.

arcade/gravitar.zip.title: Gravitar
arcade/gravitar.zip.desc: A vector game combining gravity-based space flight with planetary cave shooting, spread across a star map.

arcade/gunfight.zip.title: Gun Fight
arcade/gunfight.zip.desc: A two-player Old West duel with scrolling backgrounds and simple cover, one of the earliest arcade shooters.

arcade/indytemp.zip.title: Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom
arcade/indytemp.zip.desc: A whip-cracking adventure through the film's mine cart chase, with multiple stages and a bonus round.

arcade/lastduel.zip.title: Last Duel
arcade/lastduel.zip.desc: A vertical shooter that alternates between a spaceship and a transforming motorcycle/mech, with a road-based second phase.

arcade/llander.zip.title: Lunar Lander
arcade/llander.zip.desc: A vector-graphics landing simulation in which thrust and rotation must be balanced to touch down on a narrow pad.

arcade/mach3.zip.title: M.A.C.H. 3
arcade/mach3.zip.desc: A laserdisc arcade game mixing live-action flight footage with a sprite overlay, in jet and bomber modes.

arcade/marble.zip.title: Marble Madness
arcade/marble.zip.desc: A trackball-controlled race through isometric obstacle courses, guiding a marble past acid pools and vacuums.

arcade/mjleague.zip.title: Major League
arcade/mjleague.zip.desc: A baseball game with a behind-the-batter view and simple timing-based batting.

arcade/nbajam.zip.title: NBA Jam
arcade/nbajam.zip.desc: A two-on-two basketball game built around exaggerated dunks, three-point streaks and on-fire scoring.

arcade/nbajamr2.zip.title: NBA Jam
arcade/nbajamr2.zip.desc: Revision 2 of NBA Jam, preserved as its own ROM set.

arcade/nbajamt1.zip.title: NBA Jam
arcade/nbajamt1.zip.desc: An early tournament revision of NBA Jam.

arcade/nbajamt2.zip.title: NBA Jam
arcade/nbajamt2.zip.desc: A later tournament revision of NBA Jam.

arcade/nbajamt3.zip.title: NBA Jam
arcade/nbajamt3.zip.desc: A further tournament revision of NBA Jam.

arcade/nbajamte.zip.title: NBA Jam Tournament Edition
arcade/nbajamte.zip.desc: An expanded NBA Jam with more teams, new secret characters and a tournament structure.

arcade/nbamaxht.zip.title: NBA Maximum Hangtime
arcade/nbamaxht.zip.desc: A later NBA Jam update with additional teams and revised rules.

arcade/pitfall2.zip.title: Pitfall II: Lost Caverns
arcade/pitfall2.zip.desc: The zipped arcade Pitfall II ROM set held alongside the unpacked folder.

arcade/rampage.zip.title: Rampage
arcade/rampage.zip.desc: Three giant monsters smash buildings across North America while the military tries to stop them.

arcade/robocop.zip.title: RoboCop
arcade/robocop.zip.desc: A run-and-gun adaptation of the film, with RoboCop shooting through Old Detroit to confront ED-209.

arcade/robocopp.zip.title: RoboCop
arcade/robocopp.zip.desc: A prototype revision of Data East's RoboCop, preserved separately in the collection.

arcade/robocop2.zip.title: RoboCop 2
arcade/robocop2.zip.desc: A side-scrolling sequel based on the second film, with driving sections and a final battle against RoboCop 2.

arcade/sbasketb.zip.title: Super Basketball
arcade/sbasketb.zip.desc: A vertical basketball game with a scrolling court and simple two-on-two play.

arcade/sbrkout.zip.title: Super Breakout
arcade/sbrkout.zip.desc: An expanded Breakout with three game modes, multiple balls and moving brick walls.

arcade/scramble.zip.title: Scramble
arcade/scramble.zip.desc: A horizontal shooter with a scrolling landscape, fuel management and a six-stage mission ending at a enemy base.
arcade/scramble.zip.history: Scramble is often cited as the first side-scrolling shooter with a continuously scrolling terrain.

arcade/sf1.zip.title: Street Fighter
arcade/sf1.zip.desc: The first Street Fighter, introducing six-button pressure-pad controls and a world warrior tournament.
arcade/sf1.zip.history: Though modestly successful, Street Fighter laid the groundwork for its genre-defining sequel.

arcade/sf2.zip.title: Street Fighter II: The World Warrior
arcade/sf2.zip.desc: The eight-character fighting game that defined competitive play, with special moves, combos and a global tournament.
arcade/sf2.zip.gameplay: Each fighter has a distinct move set and a six-button layout: three punches and three kicks of varying strength. Quarter-circle and charge motions trigger special attacks.
arcade/sf2.zip.history: Designed by Akira Nishitani and Akira Yasuda, Street Fighter II ignited the 1990s fighting-game boom and remains one of the most influential games ever made.

arcade/sf2ce.zip.title: Street Fighter II': Champion Edition
arcade/sf2ce.zip.desc: A revision that makes the four boss characters playable and allows mirror matches.

arcade/sf2i.zip.title: Street Fighter II' Turbo: Hyper Fighting
arcade/sf2i.zip.desc: A faster revision of Champion Edition with new special moves and increased game speed.

arcade/superman.zip.title: Superman
arcade/superman.zip.desc: A side-scrolling Superman game in which the hero flies through Metropolis, using heat vision and super breath.

arcade/tetris.zip.title: Tetris (arcade)
arcade/tetris.zip.desc: The arcade conversion of Tetris, with a two-player competitive mode and a trackball-controlled option.

arcade/tetrist.zip.title: Tetris (Sega)
arcade/tetrist.zip.desc: Sega's Japanese arcade release of Tetris, based on the same falling-block rules.

arcade/tetrisbl.zip.title: Tetris (bootleg)
arcade/tetrisbl.zip.desc: A bootleg arcade Tetris board held in the collection. Its origin is not verified.

arcade/uccops.zip.title: Undercover Cops
arcade/uccops.zip.desc: A dystopian beat-'em-up with three playable cops, large sprites and a ruined-city setting.
